violations.title: Encryption key hard-coded in source
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.pkb declares c_encryption_key as a package constant using the plaintext string 'HR$ystem_3ncrypt10n_K3y_2024!!'. Any developer with read access to the source repository has the AES-256 key used to encrypt all employee SSNs.
violations.evidence: c_encryption_key CONSTANT RAW(32) := UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('HR$ystem_3ncrypt10n_K3y_2024!!')
violations.remediation: Move key to Oracle Wallet or DBMS_CRYPTO key store; retrieve via DBMS_CREDENTIAL or Oracle Key Vault; never store plaintext keys in source.

violations.title: SQL injection vulnerability in search_employees
violations.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.search_employees builds a dynamic SQL string via string concatenation (v_sql := '...WHERE ' || p_filter_clause). The p_filter_clause parameter is passed in from the Oracle Forms layer without sanitization.
violations.evidence: Comment in code: '-- VULNERABILITY: String concatenation instead of bind variable'
violations.remediation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries using bind variables; use DBMS_ASSERT to validate input before dynamic SQL execution.

violations.title: Weak password hashing (MD5)
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.hash_password uses DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH_MD5. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password storage. Rainbow tables trivially crack MD5 hashes.
violations.evidence: DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH(UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW(p_password), DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH_MD5)
violations.remediation: Replace with DBMS_CRYPTO SHA-256 or SHA-512 with per-user salt, or use an application-level bcrypt/Argon2 implementation.

violations.title: No brute-force protection on authentication
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate has no failed-attempt counter, no lockout, no rate limiting, and no CAPTCHA. An attacker can attempt unlimited password guesses.
violations.evidence: Procedure body has no failed_attempts counter or lockout logic
violations.remediation: Add failed_login_attempts to USER_SESSIONS or EMPLOYEES; lock account after N failures; log each failed attempt.

violations.title: Password change does not verify old password
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.change_password accepts p_old_password but does NOT compare it against the stored hash. Any authenticated session can change a user's password without knowing the current one.
violations.evidence: procedure body: p_old_password parameter accepted but not validated against stored hash
violations.remediation: Call hash_password(p_old_password) and compare against stored value before updating.

violations.title: Authentication stub — no actual password verification
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate contains a stub for password validation — the comparison between the submitted password hash and the stored credential is not implemented. Effectively any password authenticates any user.
violations.evidence: Procedure body comment: '-- TODO: compare hashed password against stored credential'
violations.remediation: Implement the hash comparison: hash_password(p_password) must equal stored USER_CREDENTIALS.password_hash.

violations.title: TOO_MANY_ROWS in authenticate picks lowest EMP_ID
violations.description: If multiple employees share a username, the EXCEPTION WHEN TOO_MANY_ROWS handler silently picks the lowest EMP_ID, potentially authenticating the wrong user.
violations.evidence: EXCEPTION WHEN TOO_MANY_ROWS THEN SELECT MIN(EMP_ID) INTO v_emp_id FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE USERNAME = p_username
violations.remediation: Enforce UNIQUE constraint on EMPLOYEES.USERNAME and raise an error on duplicate instead of silently picking one.

violations.title: Session timeout based on login time, not last activity
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.is_session_valid checks SYSDATE - LOGIN_TIME > 30 minutes. A user who is actively working will be logged out after 30 minutes regardless of activity.
violations.evidence: WHERE SYSDATE - LOGIN_TIME > 30/1440
violations.remediation: Add LAST_ACTIVITY_TIME to USER_SESSIONS; update on each authenticated action; timeout based on last activity.

violations.title: SMTP on port 25 with no encryption
violations.description: PKG_NOTIFICATION.process_queue sends emails via UTL_SMTP on port 25 (plaintext). Email content may include employee PII. No STARTTLS or SSL/TLS configured.
violations.evidence: UTL_SMTP.OPEN_CONNECTION('smtp.internal.company.com', 25)
violations.remediation: Configure SMTP over TLS (port 587 with STARTTLS or port 465 with SSL). Avoid sending PII in email bodies.

violations.title: Circular package dependency (PKG_EMPLOYEE ↔ PKG_PAYROLL)
violations.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.create_employee calls PKG_PAYROLL.create_salary_record. PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_payroll calls PKG_EMPLOYEE.is_active for validation. Oracle requires a package to be compiled before packages that depend on it; this bidirectional dependency requires a workaround (package stubs) and prevents independent testing.
violations.evidence: Comment: '-- Circular dependency with PKG_PAYROLL (salary validation)'
violations.remediation: Extract salary initialization from create_employee into a separate initialization package, or have the calling form call both packages sequentially.

violations.title: Partial commits in calculate_payroll
violations.description: PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_payroll commits every 50 employees. If the run fails at employee 250 of 1000, 200 employees have committed payroll details and 800 do not. There is no compensating rollback — the payroll run is left in a permanently inconsistent state.
violations.evidence: IF MOD(v_emp_count, 50) = 0 THEN COMMIT; END IF; inside employee processing loop
violations.remediation: Remove intermediate commits; use BULK COLLECT/FORALL for performance; wrap entire run in a single transaction; use SAVEPOINT if partial recovery is needed.

violations.title: Partial commits in run_monthly_accrual
violations.description: PKG_LEAVE.run_monthly_accrual commits every 100 employees, creating the same inconsistency risk as calculate_payroll.
violations.evidence: IF MOD(v_count, 100) = 0 THEN COMMIT; END IF; inside employee loop
violations.remediation: Same as VIO-ARCH-02: remove intermediate commits; use BULK COLLECT/FORALL.

violations.title: Business logic encoded in Oracle Forms triggers
violations.description: Hire date validation (90-day limit) is encoded in HRMS_EMPLOYEE form's WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM trigger rather than in PKG_EMPLOYEE or PKG_VALIDATION. This bypasses the rule for any non-Forms data entry path (scripts, SQL*Plus, APIs).
violations.evidence: HIRE_DATE.WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM: IF :EMPLOYEES.HIRE_DATE > SYSDATE + 90 THEN...
violations.remediation: Move all validation to PL/SQL packages; keep Oracle Forms triggers as thin delegates only.

violations.title: Hard-coded configuration values in package constants
violations.description: Multiple packages use hard-coded values that should be in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: SMTP host/port/from-address (PKG_NOTIFICATION), tax brackets (PKG_PAYROLL), FICA wage base (PKG_PAYROLL), rating label thresholds (PKG_PERFORMANCE).
violations.evidence: c_smtp_host CONSTANT VARCHAR2(100) := 'smtp.internal.company.com'; c_fica_wage_base hard-coded 168600
violations.remediation: Move all environment-specific and annually-changing values to SYSTEM_PARAMETERS table; read via PKG_COMMON.get_param.

violations.title: Row-by-row cursor processing in calculate_payroll
violations.description: PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_payroll processes employees one by one inside a cursor FOR loop. This is an Oracle anti-pattern for bulk operations ('slow-by-slow') and is documented in a TODO comment.
violations.evidence: FOR emp_rec IN (SELECT ... FROM EMPLOYEES ...) LOOP — comment: '-- TODO: refactor to BULK COLLECT/FORALL'
violations.remediation: Refactor to BULK COLLECT with FORALL INSERT for an order-of-magnitude performance improvement.

violations.title: Hard-coded pay element IDs in PKG_REPORTING
violations.description: PKG_REPORTING.payroll_summary_report uses hard-coded ELEMENT_IDs (100=federal tax, 101=state tax, 102=SS, 103=Medicare). If the PAY_ELEMENTS table is repopulated with different IDs, the report breaks silently.
violations.evidence: WHERE ELEMENT_ID IN (100, 101, 102, 103) — comment: 'Hard-coded element IDs'
violations.remediation: Join on ELEMENT_CODE or ELEMENT_NAME; never depend on surrogate key values.

violations.title: validate_required_fields only handles EMPLOYEES table
violations.description: PKG_VALIDATION.validate_required_fields has a CASE statement for p_table_name = 'EMPLOYEES' only. For all other tables the procedure does nothing, silently passing validation.
violations.evidence: CASE p_table_name WHEN 'EMPLOYEES' THEN ... ELSE NULL END; — comment: 'TODO: add other tables'
violations.remediation: Implement validation for all tables, or use a metadata-driven approach with SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.

violations.title: HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB email regex rejects valid subdomains
violations.description: The client-side email validation function in HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB.pll uses a regex that rejects valid email addresses containing subdomain dots (e.g. user@mail.company.com).
violations.evidence: Email regex: '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$' — does not allow subdomain dots in domain part
violations.remediation: Update regex to allow dots in the domain part: '@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+'.

violations.title: Hire date validation inconsistency between form and trigger
violations.description: HRMS_EMPLOYEE form validates hire date ≤ SYSDATE + 90 days. TRG_EMPLOYEES_VALIDATE allows up to SYSDATE + 180 days. An employee hired with a date 91-180 days in the future passes the DB trigger but is blocked by the form — unless data is inserted directly.
violations.evidence: Form: SYSDATE + 90; Trigger: SYSDATE + 180
violations.remediation: Choose one authoritative rule and apply it consistently in both locations, with the DB trigger as the enforcement point.

violations.title: VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY AVAILABLE formula omits PENDING days
violations.description: VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY computes AVAILABLE = BALANCE - USED. The LEAVE_BALANCES table has a virtual column AVAILABLE = BALANCE - PENDING - USED. The view omits PENDING days, making available balance appear higher than it is.
violations.evidence: VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY: ACCRUED_DAYS - USED_DAYS AS AVAILABLE_DAYS vs LEAVE_BALANCES virtual column: ACCRUED_DAYS - PENDING_DAYS - USED_DAYS
violations.remediation: Update VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY to subtract PENDING_DAYS: ACCRUED_DAYS - PENDING_DAYS - USED_DAYS AS AVAILABLE_DAYS.

violations.title: Race condition in generate_emp_number
violations.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.generate_emp_number selects MAX(EMP_NUMBER) + 1 without a SELECT FOR UPDATE. Two concurrent inserts can generate the same employee number, causing a unique constraint violation on the second commit.
violations.evidence: SELECT NVL(MAX(TO_NUMBER(EMP_NUMBER)), 0) + 1 INTO v_new_num FROM EMPLOYEES — no FOR UPDATE
violations.remediation: Replace with a SEQUENCE (already available as SEQ_EMPLOYEE) to generate employee numbers atomically.

violations.title: expire_carryover double-subtract bug
violations.description: PKG_LEAVE.expire_carryover will double-subtract carryover days if executed twice on the same day (e.g. if the scheduler fires twice due to a retry). No idempotency guard exists.
violations.evidence: Code comment: '-- BUG: if this procedure runs twice on same day, carryover is subtracted twice'
violations.remediation: Add an idempotency check: record expiry date in LEAVE_ACCRUAL_LOG; skip if already processed for this year.

violations.title: calculate_business_days does not handle observed holidays
violations.description: PKG_LEAVE.calculate_business_days queries the HOLIDAYS table but does not account for 'observed' holidays (e.g. when a holiday falls on Sunday, Monday is observed). Leave day counts may be off by one for affected date ranges.
violations.evidence: Code comment: '-- BUG: does not handle observed holidays'
violations.remediation: Add OBSERVED_DATE column to HOLIDAYS table (or a flag); update calculate_business_days to check both dates.

violations.title: Unimplemented integration stubs
violations.description: PKG_INTEGRATION contains two unimplemented procedures: import_time_attendance (CSV parsing TODO) and sync_org_structure (LDAP/AD sync placeholder). Callers receive no error — procedures return silently.
violations.evidence: import_time_attendance body: '-- TODO: implement CSV parsing'; sync_org_structure body: '-- TODO: implement LDAP sync'
violations.remediation: Either implement or raise NOT_IMPLEMENTED error; document that these features are not available.
